requirements.requirement: On node1, opsadmin exists with the specified ed25519 public key configured for SSH access (as authorized key)
requirements.summary: opsadmin did not previously exist; it was created with home/.ssh (0700) and authorized_keys (0600) containing exactly the required key with correct SELinux context (ssh_home_t). Live SSH login with the required key succeeded pre-restart, and the key persisted unchanged (single entry) through a full node restart, confirmed again post-restart.

requirements.requirement: SSH on node1 requires key-based authentication (password/interactive auth disabled)
requirements.summary: A drop-in (10-key-only.conf) sets PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no / AuthenticationMethods publickey; sshd -t validated and sshd -T confirms the effective runtime config both before and after a full restart. Live SSH tests directly demonstrate the behavior: an attempt with no matching key is rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' only, a matching-key attempt succeeds, and a password-preferred attempt is rejected, all repeated post-restart. opsadmin's password hash is also locked ('!'), reinforcing that no password path exists.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/config state on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 7ef78016... with sshd active and opsadmin locked. shutdown -r now was issued and acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls show connection timeout/reset (unreachable), then a successful poll with a new boot_id (bdd30bd8...) and new uptime. Post-restart checks confirm sshd active, opsadmin still locked, authorized_keys and sshd_config.d/10-key-only.conf intact, sshd -T unchanged, and live SSH key-auth/password-rejection retested successfully. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots (before_prepare boot-identity 7ef78016... vs after_executor boot-identity bdd30bd8...).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating opsadmin with the specified public key and enforcing key-only SSH authentication — are directly and repeatedly demonstrated via live SSH tests, config validation, and effective-config queries, both before and after a full node restart. The restart evidence protocol is well executed: a clean pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, an observed unreachable window, a changed boot_id, and full post-restart recovery of the user, key, and sshd configuration, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only blemish is a leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot command, a trivial and low-risk residue.
limitations: Live SSH verification was performed from the node itself (loopback, 127.0.0.1) via the executor's shell rather than from an external client, so external-network-path SSH behavior was not directly observed, though this does not affect the authentication-policy conclusions.
No requirement in the task instruction called for locking opsadmin's password, but this is a reasonable supporting hardening step with no negative side effects for the key-only requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: user/key creation, sshd hardening drop-in, and password lock, all with a clear causal role in satisfying the two material requirements. Two temporary SSH keypairs (cmd-5d11f417e00c411c and cmd-fe25d8aa3268431e) were added to authorized_keys purely to prove login works, then promptly removed and the file restored to the single required key (cmd-c97739f0f5404bc1, cmd-3addd321d2c248a8, cmd-1eed4db013be49da) — bounded, low-risk, fully reverted verification steps directly supporting the outcome. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, created as a redirect target for the backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' command (cmd-85be8b4c8db342ec), was left on disk after restart per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a trivial, non-sensitive log file with negligible blast radius but was not cleaned up.
